product_scope.problem_statement: The solution needs a minimum end-to-end flow that can be defended in the challenge: schedule daily work, select pending records, dispatch them for execution, call provider APIs, and persist outcomes while preserving strict per-provider isolation.
product_scope.goal: Implement the simplest correct orchestration flow that satisfies the functional core of the challenge before adding advanced resilience and scale patterns.
success_outcomes: A daily process can trigger the orchestration for a target execution date.
Pending records for the target date are selected and dispatched for execution.
Requests for the same provider are executed one at a time and in order.
Requests for different providers can progress in parallel.
Terminal provider failures are persisted as auditable outcomes.

in_scope: Daily trigger entry into the orchestration flow.
Selection of pending records for a logical target date.
Dispatch of provider work items into the execution pipeline.
Execution of one provider API call per work item.
A repository structure and domain flow that are understandable and defendable.
out_of_scope: DLQ and operational failure recovery details beyond the minimum needed to avoid ambiguity.
Large-scale segmentation, distributed map, or shuffle-sharding.

actors.name: Producer Flow
actors.description: Finds pending work for the target date and dispatches it.

actors.name: Execution Flow
actors.description: Consumes one work item at a time for a provider and calls the provider API.

actors.name: Provider API
actors.description: Receives the outgoing request for a work item.

actors.name: Technical Reviewer
actors.description: Evaluates whether the core solution is correct, coherent, and aligned with the challenge.

user_journeys.name: Daily core orchestration
steps: A scheduled event starts the orchestration for a date.
The system selects eligible pending records for that date.
The system dispatches one execution message per eligible record.
The system routes those messages through provider-aware ordering.
The system executes provider calls and persists final outcomes.

user_journeys.name: Successful provider execution
steps: A work item reaches the execution flow.
The system calls the provider endpoint using the record contract.
The system persists the successful result for audit.

user_journeys.name: Terminal failure persistence
steps: A work item reaches the execution flow.
The provider responds with a non-retryable or terminal error.
The system persists the failure outcome with enough context for review.
The item stops as a terminal result of the core flow.

user_journeys.name: Provider isolation
steps: Multiple records exist for the same provider and other providers.
The system dispatches all eligible records.
Records for the same provider are processed strictly one at a time and in order.
Records for different providers may advance concurrently.

use_cases.title: Start daily orchestration
use_cases.description: The system begins a daily run for a target date, defaulting to the current scheduled date when no override is provided.

use_cases.title: Select pending records
use_cases.description: The system retrieves eligible pending records for the target date.

use_cases.title: Dispatch work items
use_cases.description: The system publishes one execution message per eligible record using provider-aware grouping.

use_cases.title: Execute provider request
use_cases.description: The system performs the provider API call for one work item.

use_cases.title: Persist success outcome
use_cases.description: The system stores the successful provider response as a durable result.

use_cases.title: Persist terminal failure outcome
use_cases.description: The system stores a terminal failure result with enough context for technical review.

business_rules.rule: A pending record represents exactly one provider work item for one logical execution date.
Only records in pending state are eligible for dispatch in the core flow.
Every eligible record must produce exactly one dispatched execution work item in the core flow.
Records for the same provider must never execute concurrently.
Records for the same provider must preserve ordering from dispatch through execution.
Records for different providers may execute in parallel.
A successful provider response must be persisted as a result record.
A terminal provider failure must be persisted as a failure result record.
This phase must prefer clarity and correctness of the core flow over advanced optimization.
The core flow must stay explainable as the foundation for later resilience and scale phases.

functional_requirements.title: Daily trigger
functional_requirements.statement: The system must support a scheduled entrypoint that starts the core orchestration flow once per day.

functional_requirements.title: Target-date support
functional_requirements.statement: The system must support resolving the logical date whose pending work is being processed.

functional_requirements.title: Pending record selection
functional_requirements.statement: The system must retrieve eligible pending records for the target date.

functional_requirements.title: Dispatch of execution work
functional_requirements.statement: The system must dispatch one execution work item per eligible pending record.

functional_requirements.title: Provider-level serialization
functional_requirements.statement: The system must serialize execution for each provider.

functional_requirements.title: Cross-provider parallelism
functional_requirements.statement: The system must allow execution progress across different providers at the same time.

functional_requirements.title: Provider request execution
functional_requirements.statement: The system must perform the provider request described by the dispatched work item.

functional_requirements.title: Success persistence
functional_requirements.statement: The system must persist successful provider outcomes.

functional_requirements.title: Terminal failure persistence
functional_requirements.statement: The system must persist terminal provider failures.

functional_requirements.title: Core flow traceability
functional_requirements.statement: The system must make the path from scheduled trigger to final persisted outcome understandable in code and tests.

interaction_expectations.expectation: A reviewer should be able to follow the core flow end-to-end without ambiguity about which component is responsible for selection, dispatch, execution, and persistence.
The core phase should avoid redundant handlers or split mental models that make the architecture harder to explain.
The code should establish a stable foundation for later resilience and scale phases instead of hiding future complexity in the core path.

acceptance_criteria.then: The system resolves a target execution date and begins processing pending work for that date.

acceptance_criteria.given: There are pending records for the target date
acceptance_criteria.then: The system dispatches one execution work item per eligible pending record.

acceptance_criteria.given: There are no pending records for the target date
acceptance_criteria.then: The system completes without dispatching execution work.

acceptance_criteria.given: Two or more dispatched items belong to the same provider
acceptance_criteria.then: They are processed one at a time and in order.

acceptance_criteria.given: Dispatched items belong to different providers
acceptance_criteria.then: They may progress in parallel without violating same-provider isolation.
The system persists a successful result record.

acceptance_criteria.given: A provider call fails with a terminal outcome
acceptance_criteria.then: The system persists a failure result record.

acceptance_criteria.when: They trace the core orchestration path
acceptance_criteria.then: They can map scheduler, producer, execution, and persistence responsibilities without relying on implicit behavior.

assumptions: This phase optimizes for a correct and explainable core flow, not for complete production hardening.
Advanced retries, idempotency persistence, and massive-scale segmentation will be handled in later phases.
The core phase may reuse ideas or selected modules from the current repository, but it is free to simplify or replace them for clarity.
A target-date override remains useful for manual runs and testability.

open_questions.question: Should the core flow keep a separate orchestrator component between queue consumption and provider execution, or collapse execution responsibilities for simplicity if that improves explainability?
Should pending-record state transitions beyond PENDING be part of the core flow now, or deferred until resilience and idempotency are specified in phase 2?
